subject: Surge readiness & pricing next steps
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Ellis Park <ellis@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Surge readiness & pricing next steps

Hi Ellis — great conversation earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Call summary (TL;DR)
- Primary workload: transaction enrichment + multi-turn summarization for realtime dashboards.
- Baseline expected volume: 12–18M tokens/month.
- Peak pattern observed on call: up to ~3.5–4.0M tokens/day during business hours; short spikes up to 10–12M tokens in a few hourly windows during product launches.
- Initial budget range you indicated: $8k–$15k/month, open to trading committed capacity for lower unit price.

Pricing & unit economics we discussed
- Typical target we see for customers at this stage: $150–$250 per 1M tokens for reserved capacity; on-demand/overage often runs $260–$350/1M depending on model family and quantization.
- For quick planning, if you target $200/1M and baseline 15M tokens/mo, monthly cost ~ $3,000 before egress/other add-ons. Spikes will change the blended rate.

Rate limits, burst behavior, and overage model
- Baseline quota: we size committed capacity by monthly tokens + a sustained per-minute allowance (we'll propose a starting sustained cap).
- Burst window: short bursts (up to 5–10 minutes) are allowed at higher headroom; typical soft-burst allowance is ~8x sustained for up to 5 minutes, with soft-throttle thereafter.
- Overage pricing: when you exceed the monthly committed tokens, we charge overage at an agreed rate (we typically propose $260–$320/1M tokens for on-demand overage by default).
- Emergency throttles: to protect cluster health, extremely large spikes (>> burst allowance) will be soft-throttled and we notify the customer.

What I will do next (deliverables from Redwood)
1) Send a simple pricing quote with 2 options (Reserved + Surge add-on, and On-demand) — attaching a draft spreadsheet.
2) Provide a sample 7‑day usage CSV based on the pattern you shared so you can model blended cost.
3) Outline the quota increase / approval process (timeline + contacts) so you can plan launches.

What I need from you
- Confirm whether the 12–18M/mo baseline is the right planning band. If we should plan higher (20–30M) call that out.
- Confirm target unit $/1M (rough target helps us craft an offer).
- Any procurement constraints (PO required, 30/45/60 day terms) or security docs needed early.

Next steps
- I propose a short 30-minute follow-up Tue 04/20 to go through a quote and pick a path.
- If that works, I’ll loop in our procurement lead and solutions SE.

Attachment: [Attachment: redwood-pricing-quote-finbot-20270417.xlsx (xlsx, 31KB)]
Attachment: [Attachment: usage-sample-finbot.csv (csv, 6KB)]

Thanks — enjoyed the product detail you shared.

— Ava Chen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

From: Ellis Park <ellis@finbot.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Patricia Gomez <patricia.gomez@finbot.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2027 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Surge readiness & pricing next steps

Hi Ava — thanks for the recap and the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Baseline & spikes
- 15M/mo is a fair planning baseline for Q2; we expect a growth ramp to 30M/mo over next 6 months if retention targets hold.
- The 10–12M spike number is accurate for marketing-driven releases (we saw this last quarter).

2) Budget and target unit economics
- Our procurement target is closer to $200–$250 per 1M tokens if possible. We can stretch to $300/1M for short-term on-demand overage during launches.
- Initial procurement budget for POC/testing is $10k–12k/month. If we see predicted ROI we can expand to the higher band you mention.

3) Procurement & compliance
- We require a PO and prefer Net-45 payment terms.
- SOC 2 Type II and a list of sub-processors would be required before any dedicated/private deployment.

4) Follow-up
- Tue 04/20 10:00am PT works for a short call with our engineering lead and Patricia (cc).

Thanks, Ellis
Ellis Park
Head of Product | FinBot
ellis@finbot.ai | +1 (206) 555-0147

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Surge readiness & pricing next steps — proposed offer

Ava / Ben — quick internal note I drafted for the quote we send tomorrow. I tried to align with Ellis's $200–$250 target while protecting unit economics. Suggestions welcome.

Proposal (compact)
Option A — Reserved + Surge add-on (recommended for predictable cost)
- Committed baseline: 15M tokens/month at $180 / 1M tokens (monthly charge = $2,700)
- Surge add-on: additional pool charged at $260 / 1M tokens, with an 8x soft-burst cap (up to 8M tokens/5min) before soft-throttle.
- Overage after add-on (monthly): $300 / 1M tokens.
- PO + Net-45 accepted; 30-day trial credit of 2M tokens to validate integration.

Option B — On-demand (no commitment)
- Pay-as-you-go at $300 / 1M tokens; burst allowed but subject to dynamic throttle and higher overage rates.

Operational notes
- Quota increase process: submit request to account team + solutions SE; staging test window for 48–72 hours; production ramp plan usually 3–7 business days for moderate increases, signed amendment required for >50% committed increase.
- SLA: standard hosted SLA included; Private/VPC requires enterprise contract.

Attachments included in external quote: pricing spreadsheet, sample usage CSV, and a short doc on quota/process.

If you approve, I’ll incorporate Ben’s commercial ask (intro discount) and we can send this to FinBot.

— Neha
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2027 10:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Surge readiness & pricing next steps — approval to include pilot discount

Thanks — good structure. Approve moving forward with Option A as the recommended path. A couple commercial notes: 
- Approve a one-time promotional credit equal to 10% of first three months if FinBot signs a 12-month commitment at >=100M tokens/year.
- Approve an initial 2M token trial credit (as Neha suggested).
- We should explicitly call out the ramp timeline and require a signed amendment for quota >50% of baseline.

Cc'ing rishi for visibility on discounts.

Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Surge readiness & pricing next steps

Hi Ellis / Patricia — thanks for confirming the time on Tue 04/20 10:00am PT. Attached is the formal quote and a short usage sample to help model blended costs. Key points below so you have a single-page view: 

Offer summary (attached spreadsheet)
- Recommended: Reserved + Surge add-on
- 15M tokens/mo reserved @ $180/1M ($2,700/mo)
- Surge add-on charged at $260/1M for additional pool; soft-burst allowance up to ~8x sustained for short windows (configurable, we recommend 5 minutes default)
- Monthly overage after add-on billed at $300/1M
- One-time promotional: 10% credit on first 3 months if FinBot signs a 12-mo commit >=100M tokens/yr
- Trial credit: 2M tokens to validate end-to-end integration

Quota & ramp process (operational)
- For increases up to 50% of baseline we can approve within 3–7 business days after a short staging test (48–72h).
- For increases >50% we require a signed amendment and typical lead time is 7–14 business days depending on capacity reservations.
- Emergency bursts beyond the configured soft-burst window will be soft-throttled; we’ll send alerting/telemetry to your SRE during those events.

Procurement
- We accept PO and Net-45, but enterprise contracts with Private/VPC deployments require additional security review (SOC 2 Type II / sub-processor list). I’ve attached the SOC 2 factsheet to the HubSpot deal — we’ll surface it on the call.

Next steps
1) Call Tue 04/20 10:00am PT — I’ll share a short agenda and invite.
2) If FinBot wants to proceed with Reserved path after the call, we’ll prepare a DocuSign amendment reflecting the committed tokens and promotional credit.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-quote-finbot-20270417.xlsx, usage-sample-finbot.csv
